_note: Copy to ~/.cherrypick/config/desk.json. Every default is the SAFE one: an absent or empty file refuses every order. This config authorizes HUMAN-INITIATED orders only and is completely independent of every module's enable_live_trading — enabling the desk never enables an automated loop, and vice versa.
_enabled_note: The desk's own master switch. Nothing is submitted while this is false. Deliberately separate from any module flag so the two can never be conflated.
_allowed_accounts_note: Last-4 fragments of the accounts authorized for manual orders, e.g. ["2375"]. Full account numbers never appear here (suite-wide masking rule); matching is done against the last 4 of the account resolved at submit time. An empty list refuses everything.
_require_defined_risk_note: Refuse any OPENING order whose loss is unbounded (net short the upside tail) or not computable (a calendar/diagonal, where a single-expiry payoff is the wrong model). Set false to permit them — the dollar cap below still applies, and an uncomputable worst case can never satisfy a finite cap, so you must also null the cap to allow one through. CLOSING orders are exempt: flattening a naked short is exactly what you never want to block.
_max_order_risk_dollars_note: Worst case at expiry, in dollars, that a single OPENING order may risk. Computed from the payoff diagram, not from a strategy-name whitelist. Set to null to disable the cap entirely — an ABSENT key falls back to 500, so forgetting it can never disable it. Closing orders are exempt.
_ticket_ttl_seconds_note: How long a proposed order stays confirmable. Long enough to read the review and answer, short enough that an abandoned proposal cannot be revived later from scrollback.
_daily_caps_note: Optional brakes, OFF unless set. Counted from the audit journal's `submitted` events only — a refused or merely proposed order consumes no budget. Useful as a runaway backstop.
_broker_keyring_service_note: Which existing module's keyring service holds the broker OAuth credentials to trade through. The desk stores NO secrets of its own — duplicating them into a second keyring entry would double the leak surface for no added capability. Borrowing the credentials is not borrowing the permissions: the desk never reads that module's trading flags.
